seo.title: Ads on Apple Maps: How Local Businesses Advertise
seo.meta_description: How Anaheim and Orange County businesses can promote locations with ads on Apple Maps through Apple Business: setup, locations, monthly budgets and eligibility.

h1: Ads on Apple Maps: How to Promote Your Business With Apple Business
answer: Ads on Apple Maps let businesses promote their locations to people searching in Apple Maps, set up through Apple Business. You choose up to three assets, the locations to promote and a monthly budget maximum. Apple says ads on Maps are available in the United States and Canada for advertisers with locations there. Anaheim and Orange County businesses can use them to reach iPhone users nearby.
key_takeaways: Available in the U.S. and Canada.
Choose up to three assets per ad.
Currency and time zone can't be changed later.

sections.heading: Apple Business Connect is now Apple Business
sections.body_html: Apple's guide states that Apple Business Connect is now Apple Business, which combines what was previously in Apple Business Manager, Apple Business Essentials and Apple Business Connect into one offering. If you used Apple Business Connect before, you can sign in to Apple Business with the same personal Apple Account.

sections.heading: Who can advertise
sections.body_html: Apple's guide says ads on Maps are available in the United States, excluding American Samoa and the Northern Mariana Islands, and Canada. Only advertisers with business locations and an organization address in those countries are eligible.

sections.heading: Step 1: Apple Business
sections.body_html: Start by signing up for Apple Business, verifying your organization, claiming your locations and uploading photos. The ads use the locations and photos you've already set up.

sections.heading: Step 2: organization details
sections.body_html: In Apple Business, select Ads, agree to the Apple Advertising Services Terms of Service and add your organization details. Apple warns that the currency and time zone can't be changed later, so set them carefully. You'll also enter your legal entity name, address and tax ID status.

sections.heading: Step 3: create an ad
sections.body_html: Name the ad, choose up to three assets and optionally add promotional text. A preview shows roughly how the ad will look, and you can swap assets before saving.

sections.heading: Step 4: choose locations
sections.body_html: Promote all locations for the broadest coverage, which also includes locations you add later, or pick specific ones. A business with several Orange County locations might promote only the ones that need more customers.

sections.heading: Step 5: monthly budget
sections.body_html: Set a maximum monthly budget, either a suggested amount or your own. You can start or stop the campaign at any time, and it keeps spending within the monthly budget unless paused. Apple says some organizations may be eligible for a one-time $150 USD sign-up credit, subject to eligibility and terms.

sections.heading: Step 6: review and launch
sections.body_html: Review the ad preview, chosen locations and budget, add a payment method and launch.

sections.heading: Photos matter
sections.body_html: Apple says photos in location campaigns are subject to its photo and text standards and advertising policies. Clean, real photos of your location work best.

sections.heading: Measure results
sections.body_html: Use Apple's reporting together with Apple Business insights and your own records of calls and visits. Compare cost with the customers it brings, not just views.

sections.heading: Common mistakes
sections.body_html:
• Choosing the wrong currency or time zone.
  • Advertising before the place card is complete.
  • Promoting locations with poor reviews or photos.
  • No way to track calls and visits.
  • Setting a budget and never reviewing it.

sections.heading: Questions owners ask us
sections.body_html: Owners often ask whether Apple Maps ads are worth it compared with Google Ads. It depends on how many of your customers use iPhones and Apple Maps, which you can estimate from Apple Business insights before spending. A small test budget for a month or two shows whether ads bring calls and visits at a reasonable cost. Another common question is whether ads affect organic placement. Apple's guide describes ads as a separate way to promote locations; keep your place card complete regardless. Owners also ask about the sign-up credit. Apple says eligibility limits and terms apply, so check what's offered when you set up.

sections.heading: Checklist
sections.body_html:
• Apple Business set up and verified.
  • Place card complete with photos.
  • Currency and time zone set correctly.
  • Up to three good assets chosen.
  • Locations selected.
  • Monthly budget set and reviewed.

sections.heading: An example
sections.body_html: Imagine a tire shop with locations in Anaheim and Orange that wants more walk-in customers. After completing its place cards and photos, it creates an ad with three photos of its service bays and storefront, promotes only the newer Orange location, and sets a modest monthly budget. After two months, it compares calls and visits with the budget before deciding whether to expand.

sections.heading: How this fits your local plan
sections.body_html: This task is one piece of a wider local plan. Google says local results are mainly based on relevance, distance and popularity, so the profile, your website and your reputation all have to agree. A practical order for most Orange County businesses is: get the Business Profile verified and accurate, make the name, address and phone identical everywhere, publish one clear page per service, then build a steady habit of genuine reviews and replies. Each step makes the next one work better, and the same signals help AI assistants such as ChatGPT, Gemini and Google's AI features describe your business correctly when someone in Anaheim asks for a recommendation.

sections.heading: What to do this week
sections.body_html:
1. Check your Apple Business insights.
  2. Complete place card photos.
  3. Set up Ads with the right currency and time zone.
  4. Start with a small monthly budget.

sections.heading: When to get help
sections.body_html: Most of this can be done in-house with an hour or two and careful reading of Google's own help pages. It is worth bringing in help when the stakes are high or the problem keeps coming back: a profile that has been suspended more than once, many locations to manage, a site that keeps failing the same checks, or no time to keep up the routine. A good local SEO partner should explain what they will change and why, point to Google's guidelines rather than promise rankings, and leave you with access to every account. Chimera works this way with businesses across Anaheim and Orange County.

sections.heading: Running a sensible test
sections.body_html: Treat your first Apple Maps campaign as a test. Before starting, note your current monthly calls, directions requests and website taps from Apple Business insights, and your bookings or sales from your own records. Run the campaign for one or two months with a modest monthly maximum, promoting the location that most needs customers. Afterwards, compare the same numbers and calculate a rough cost per extra call or visit. If the result is better than your other advertising, increase the budget gradually; if not, improve photos and offers or pause. Keep the place card complete throughout, since ads send people to it. This simple approach avoids spending heavily before you know whether Apple Maps users are a strong audience for your Orange County business.

sections.heading: The short version
sections.body_html: Complete Apple Business first, then create an ad with up to three assets, choose locations, set a monthly cap and measure real results. Chimera, based in Anaheim, plans Apple and Google map advertising for Orange County businesses.

faqs.q: Can I advertise on Apple Maps?
faqs.a: Yes, through Apple Business, if you have locations in the U.S. or Canada.

faqs.q: How many assets can an ad use?

faqs.a: As a maximum monthly budget, which you can start or stop anytime.

faqs.q: Can I change the currency later?
faqs.a: No. Apple says currency and time zone can't be changed later.
Apple says some organizations may be eligible for a one-time $150 USD credit; terms apply.

faqs.q: Do I need Apple Business first?
faqs.a: Yes. Ads use the locations and photos set up there.

faqs.q: Do you help businesses in Anaheim and Orange County with this?
faqs.a: Yes. Chimera is based in Anaheim, California and works with businesses across Orange County, California.
